observations.classification: native source contract corroborating existing historical observations, not a new finding
observations.trace: Reducer macro generated invoke points to rt::invoke_reducer; runtime decodes BSATN and calls reducer, whose tuple adapter invokes the original and converts its result via IntoReducerResult. Result<(),E:Display> formats E into Box<str>; sink code writes message bytes. View macro selects context dispatcher, and Vec/Option ViewReturn serialize row data; query paths use separate RawSql. The SDK later decodes its received reducer error payload as BSATN String and distinguishes internal error; the intervening host translation is not shown by these snippets.
observations.qualification: No macro expansion, client generation, host decode/transaction, database operations or actual network run. Early application error erasure remains separately scoped.

observations.classification: existing historical native observation under roles495/2477, not a new count
observations.condition: A Timestamp constructed with i64::MIN is later passed to to_duration_since_unix_epoch.
observations.trace: Public from_micros_since_unix_epoch accepts i64 without a narrower check. The conversion negates a negative signed microsecond value before casting, so the mathematical negation of the minimum is not representable in i64. Behavior depends on overflow-check configuration.
observations.qualification: The first-party clock uses the microsecond getter, not the duration conversion: this does not establish the condition or any failure. The ABI timestamp u64-to-i64 cast may encode signed bits; host contract and supported ranges are unproved.

observations.classification: conditional native/current source lifecycle question; not established defect or new count
observations.condition: If the selected pending authorization request is actually processed and argument serialization fails, or the send channel is already None at send time.
observations.trace: Generated authorization client invokes SDK with callback. The SDK queues the request and returns Ok, then later serializes args and stores the callback before checking the send channel. Apply failure propagates through advance_one_message/frame_tick; selected dispatcher logs its connection error and breaks. In the displayed failure branches no reducer-result callback is invoked; callback table cleanup, connection shutdown and supported cancellation/retry expectations remain unexamined.
observations.qualification: No actual request, disconnection, serialization failure, command spawn, retained-resource leak or player outcome was observed. Serialization failure occurs before callback storage; absent send channel occurs after storage. The exact policy and all cleanup paths require additional source evidence.

bounded_nonfindings: A successful SDK reducer callback and rejected/internal-error callbacks take distinct native paths; do not equate plain error text with an internal transport failure.
Native view Option<T> intentionally serializes a zero-or-one row collection. This alone cannot establish whether a given application None incorrectly masks an error.
Identical native bytes link roles23/495/2477 and24/491, but neither imply a new finding count nor transfer a historical lens or reviewer receipt.
Application clock getter use does not call the native duration conversion in the displayed source.
SDK formatting of E:Display at its actual reducer port is not by itself an internal application error-owner violation.
open_questions: What exact host timestamp ABI bit interpretation, legitimate range, application producer/consumer paths and compiler overflow configuration apply? Does any supported first-party path call the negative-duration conversion?
What translation exists between the module raw error sink and the SDK BSATN reducer error payload, and which consumer distinguishes local transport status, reducer rejection and internal error?

When queued sends fail, what are complete callback cleanup, shutdown, user notification, retry/cancellation and resource policies? Does the selected authorization path reach the condition under a supported lifecycle?
What transaction, isolation, external-side-effect and malformed wire guarantees belong to the actual host? No output in these source windows validates those behaviors.
Which feature graph and deployment use of the four locked packages and generated bindings applies? Hashes/lock entries do not resolve features or prove execution.
